## LEGH-0622 [必须]

## LEGH-0623 [必须]
判据: The clause must include a basket (deductible) set at "0.5% of the total contract value".

## LEGH-0625 [必须]
判据: The core limitation of liability cap must be explicitly defined as "the total fees paid by the Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
提示: The prompt gives a precise, non-standard formula for the liability cap ("fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim"). ## LEGH-0626 [建议]
判据: The response must include the explicit phrase "Customer will indemnify the Service Provider Indemnitees from any damages".
提示: While the prompt asks to "limit liability," applying that cap to everything is legally inaccurate and commercially nonsensical. Indemnities for third-party claims and liabilities for gross negligence or wilful misconduct are standard, critical carve-outs. A response that ignores this, while technically following the "limit" instruction, produces a legally defective and unenforceable clause.
出处: prbench:048bc494b360641675783c78 | 话题: Corporate & Transactional Law

## LEGH-0720 [必须]
判据: The response states that aside from the procedural question of when to file a petition with the UN, the model will proceed to answer the user's substantive questions.
提示: This criterion addresses an error in the original prompt. The user asks about a UN petition, which is a document that is only used in the area of human rights and not International Humanitarian Law. For procedural correctness, the model needs to note that the scenario presented in the prompt would not give rise to a petition, but it should also proceed with answering the rest of the user's questions. (For purposes of naturalness, this was an actual error that I made when I forget to full edit an earlier prompt, and not something I added to try and trick the model. Since it led to a question of procedural correctness, I decided to leave it in.)
出处: prbench:d61354fc68bcf51b7f279dfc | 话题: International Law & Trade

## LEGH-0721 [负面]
判据: The response suggests treaty sections that can only be used to argue for animal protection if the animals are classified as "civilian objects" (which are defined as all objects that do not qualify as military objectives and include civilian property and objects essential to human survival even if the treaty does not specifically refer to them as civilian objects), such as Article 54(1) of the Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions.
提示: Providing such treaty sections directly violates the prompt and shows a lack of understanding of the definition of civilian objects, which, regardless of the terminology used in the treaty, includes civilian property and objects necessary to human survival. It would be impossible include a comprehensive list of all treaty provisions dealing either explicitly or implicitly with civilian objects, but the Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions Articles 54(1) is the one that is commonly invoked to argue for animal protection and is the one that should be explicitly excluded here.
出处: prbench:d61354fc68bcf51b7f279dfc | 话题: International Law & Trade

## LEGH-0722 [必须]
判据: The response acknowledges that the user is not interested in making arguments based on the classification of animals as "civilian objects" (which is defined as all objects that do not qualify as military objectives and includes civilian property and objects essential to human survival even if the treaty does not specifically refer to them as civilian objects).
提示: Though it is not absolutely critical that the response explicitly acknowledge this part of the prompt, some form of acknowledgement that the user does not want to consider this type of argument adds clarity to the response and confirms that the model has understood the prompt.
出处: prbench:d61354fc68bcf51b7f279dfc | 话题: International Law & Trade
